bull_bear.body: Dividend increased to INR 3.50/share (from INR 3.00); Debt reduction prioritized (Net Debt INR 550 cr); Strategic M&A integration complete (SCS, LDC); Focus on sweating assets in Lighting division.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Middle East geopolitical conflict impacting supply chain and TRIFA sales; Commodity price volatility (Moly, Tungsten) if pass-through fails; Customer project launch delays; Tariff regulation changes.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and decisive; Emphasis on 'heavy lifting' of restructuring being complete; Pragmatic on external risks (Middle East, commodities); Strategic shift from 'cable player' to 'mechatronics/solutions' provider.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Consolidated PBT exceeded Standalone PBT for the first time, marking a structural shift in earnings mix towards global subsidiaries; Renaming of divisions (DCD->ICM, SCD->GCM, PLD->PLE) signals strategic pivot to mechatronics and electricals beyond pure cables; 'Last Man Standing' strategy in lighting benefiting from competitor insolvency in Europe.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Group debt is disclosed as Long Term 2,238 (Mar-26) to 2,199 (June-26) and Short Term 5,612 to 5,556, with the deck's own Total moving 7,850 to 7,755 (Million INR).
- Group investment in mutual funds and bonds moved from 2,365 (Mar-26) to 2,431 (June-26) (Million INR).
- Growth ambition is framed as a margin-preserving target rather than a capex number: "We target to grow our consolidated business by 5-10% better than global industry growth (5-year average) – while maintaining our strong double-digit margins."
- Deck explains the higher consolidated Effective Tax Rate as arising from "losses in some of the subsidiaries" and deferred tax assets in a few subsidiaries "not recognized on a prudent basis".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: GCM (ex-SCD+SCS): Revenue +10% (ex-SCS), Margin improved to 11% (ex-SCS), SCS turned EBITDA positive (+2% in Q4); ICM (ex-DCD): Revenue +9% (impacted by price concessions), underlying volume strong, margins robust; SED: Revenue +20%, strong momentum in digital clusters/throttle controls; PLE (ex-PLD): Revenue -3%, margin pressure from commodity costs and Middle East conflict affecting TRIFA brand.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Turnaround of distressed SCS asset and global restructuring proving execution capability | Suprajit Engineering Ltd | beneficiary | High | SCS turned EBITDA positive in Q4 FY26; GCM margin guidance jumps to 10-12% from 6%. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Deck claims Suprajit "started supplying mechanical control cables in 1985 and is today arguably the largest manufacturer of control cables in the world (by volume) producing more than 300 million cables a year", with 20+ cable applications in a car and 5+ in 2-wheelers and off-highway vehicles.
- Also states it is "the third largest manufacturer of halogen lamps globally by volume, producing over 80 million lamps per year", majorly an aftermarket product in India and globally.
- Long-stated policy is to "De-Risk and grow Profitably", supported by a global footprint "leveraging onshore, nearshore, and offshore models" for US and Europe based on customer risk-value-benefit.
- Market diversification across Passenger Vehicle, Off-Highway, 2 & 3-Wheeler and Aftermarket means "no customer of has more than 10% of Suprajit revenue" (deck's wording); it supplies a majority of OEMs and Tier-1s across India, US and Europe.
- EV readiness framed as products being "generally Drivetrain/EV agnostic as control cables are usually the lowest cost option for actuation", with speedometer/throttle cable erosion "mitigated by our SED product portfolio".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Corrigendum] The 7 August 2026 filing corrects the 6 August 2026 press release and presentation: "Phoenix Lamps & Electricals (PLE)" should be read as "Phoenix Lighting & Electricals (PLE)"; the company confirms no change in the substance of the disclosure.
- [Division renaming] New nomenclature: PLD is now PLE, SCD is now GCM, DCD is now ICM, SED stays SED; divisions are now defined by customer geography/product rather than legacy names.
- [Reporting change] "As informed in the earlier Press Release, SCS financials are now clubbed with GCM"; previous year's figures have been regrouped and consolidated/GCM figures include SCS.
- [Guidance] "The overall guidance provided in the earlier Press Release dated 25th May 2026 holds good, despite cost push inflation, for the year"; the margin impact in ICM and PLE is "expected to be temporary".
- [Tariffs / macro] "Various tariff recoveries from customers and government agencies are ongoing", against a backdrop of Middle East conflict, higher oil and commodity prices, trade restrictions, a global shipping crisis, and wage increases with labour shortages in India.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: FY26 margin pressure from commodity inflation (Moly, Tungsten) and lagged price concessions in India; FY27 margin expansion (400 bps for GCM) driven by operational restructuring (factory consolidation in Mexico, warehouse shifts in Europe) and full-year contribution of turned-around SCS; Tariff recoveries expected to be fully realized.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue: Double-digit growth FY27; Margin: 12%-13.5% Consolidated EBITDA (GCM specifically guided 10%-12%); Order Inflow: Strong wins in EV clusters, throttle controls, and US retailer; Capex: INR 200 cr allocated.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Strong double-digit growth in India and China operations; Specific monetary value undisclosed but described as 'strong' with new wins in premium EV motorbikes and US off-highway.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Beyond-Cables: Brake calipers (TCA signed), Sunroof cables, ABS (with Bluebrake); EV Electronics: Complete clusters/throttle/switch assembly for premium EV bikes; US Retailer channel expansion for electrical products; Market share gains from insolvent global halogen competitor.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Suprajit crossed INR 1,000 cr quarterly revenue with consolidated PBT doubling YoY, driven by the successful EBITDA turnaround of acquired SCS and global restructuring. FY27 guidance targets double-digit revenue growth and 12-13.5% EBITDA margins, leveraging operational fixes in Mexico/Europe and new wins in EV electronics and braking systems.
